traits.spine_cover.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Mammillaria prolifera var. texana, 'hair-covered cactus': 'tubercles 7-10 × 3.4-5 mm; axils mostly bearing sparse white hairs and slender bristles equaling or exceeding tubercle length. Spines 30-50 per areole ... radial spines 25-40 per areole, white to pale yellow, hairlike, 3-12 × 0.01-0.02 mm, soft'; Britton and Rose, The Cactaceae vol. 4 (1923), p. 124, Neomammillaria prolifera: 'axils of tubercles with long, hair-like bristles; radial spines many, hair-like', and Plumier's 'Melocactus minimus, lanuginosus' (woolly). Thirty to fifty hairlike spines up to 12 mm long on tubercles 3.4-5 mm wide, with axillary hairs and bristles, nearly hide the stem, as the plant's name says; the share is the model's reading of the words.

traits.stem_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Mammillaria prolifera var. texana: plants branched; branches 5-20+. Roots fibrous. Stems spheric to cylindric-clavate, 3-9 × 1.2-5 cm, somewhat flaccid; tubercles 7-10 × 3.4-5 mm; axils mostly bearing sparse white hairs and slender bristles equaling or exceeding tubercle length. Spines 30-50 per areole, white to yellow or reddish sometimes tipped dark, puberulent; radial spines 25-40 per areole, white to pale yellow, hairlike, 3-12 × 0.01-0.02 mm, soft, strongly contrasting with relatively rigid, colored central spines; central spines 5-12 per areole, spreading in all directions, straight, 4-9 × 0.11-0.17 mm. Flowers 1-1.8 × 0.8-1.7 cm; inner tepals whitish to creamy yellowish with pinkish or greenish brown midstripes; stigma lobes whitish to yellowish. Fruits bright red, obovoid to clavate-cylindric, 8-20 × 4-5 mm. Flowering spring (Mar-May). The bristles as long as the tubercles; colours by hand from the words.

traits.fruiting_months.note: No flora read gives the months (Flora of North America vol. 4, var. texana: flowering spring (Mar-May), no fruiting). iNaturalist research-grade wild records annotated as fruiting (its API, counted 2026-10-19 for round 5): 36 over the species' range, by month Jan 5, Feb 2, Mar 3, Apr 2, May 0, Jun 0, Jul 2, Aug 4, Sep 7, Oct 5, Nov 4, Dec 2; the span of months holding at least a third of the busiest month's records, August to March. The 17 from Texas spread the same way (Sep 4, Mar 3). So the fruit ripen from late summer and persist through winter, ripe beside the next spring's first flowers, as the Flora of North America says Mammillaria fruit 'sometimes remain on the plants for months', and as its spring-flowering species fruit (M. heyderi: flowering Mar-May, fruiting Oct-Mar). Until round 5 no months were stated, so every ring mixed buds, flowers and fruit all year.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from the flora's words: a mound of a dozen or more small, soft heads under a haze of white hairlike spines, a ring of small cream flowers below each apex. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: A rough head height: about 6 cm by 10 years. Wide tolerance.

appearance.note: Hairlike radials drawn at the thinnest a spine may be, curling a little; the coloured centrals spread all round ('spreading in all directions').
